chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim al-Ashal, from al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) touch the hands of the women when they pledged their allegiance to him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He called for his bowl in which he used to perform ablution, so he poured water into it, then immersed his right hand. So every time one of them pledged her allegiance, he said to her: 'Immerse your hand.' So she would immerse just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had immersed. Thus, this was his 'touching' of their hands.' Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to it.

key_terms.مَاسَحَ: To touch or wipe over (ritual context)

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad perform the ritual touching (masah) during the pledging of allegiance by women?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific mode of 'masah' (rubbing/touching) employed by the Prophet during the pledge of allegiance to women, distinguishing it from full physical contact by utilizing a vessel of water for ablution. By instructing each woman to immerse her hand in the same water, the Imam establishes a ritualistic connection that serves as a valid form of bay'ah while maintaining modesty, a practice highly relevant to Shia jurisprudence regarding gender interaction in religious contracts.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Aslam Al Jably, from Abdul Rahman Bin Salim Al Ashal, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabaliy from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim al-Ashal from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘How did the Messenger of Allah touch the hands of women for their pledge of allegiance? He (the Imam) said, ‘He (the Messenger of Allah) asked for a bucket in which he would make wudu. He (the Messenger of Allah) poured water in it, then immersed his right hand in water and as soon as one of them pledged allegiance he (the Messenger of Allah) asked her to immerse her hand in the water and she did so whenever he (the Messenger of Allah), O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, did and this is how he touched their hands.’” Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain persons of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.
